MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  JUNE 14, 2016

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:07 p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL
City Council Members Present: Huff, Schmitz, Zuckerman
City Council Members Absent: Mitchell, Zerunyan

City Staff Present:  City Manager Doug Prichard
  Deputy City Attorney Kane Thuyen
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Community Services Direct Andy Clark
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis

Others Present:  Ritu Portugal, Park and Activities Commission

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

  NONE

5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF MAY 24, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF MAY 24, 2016 AS
  PRESENTED.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz
  ABSENT:  Mitchell, Zerunyan
  ABSTAIN:  Zuckerman*

  *MAYOR ZUCKERMAN DID NOT ATTEND THIS MEETING.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – MAY AND JUNE

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 56905 THROUGH 56943 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $274,998.59; SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 043016; 050116 THROUGH
  050216; 56748 THROUGH 56759; 56804 (VOID); 56808 56828; 55869
  THROUGH 56882 IN THE AMOUNT OF $214,066.83 FOR A GRAND
  TOTAL AMOUNT OF $489,065.42 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell, Zerunyan

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
JUNE 14, 2016
 6.  CONSENT CALENDAR: The following routine matters will be acted upon by one
  vote to approve with the majority consent of the City Council. There will be no
  separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior
  to the roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)\

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE ITEM A.

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to

  read by title only.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

  JUNE 6, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE ADJOURNED PARK AND ACTIVITIES
  COMMISSION MINUTES OF MAY 16, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

10.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  BID RESULTS – RESURFACING PROJECT ON VARIOUS CITY STREETS AND
  MULTI-USE PEDESTRIAN PATHS

  Recommendation: That the City Council award the bid to All American Asphalt in
  the amount of $1,039,695 for the 2016 Resurfacing Project on Various City
  Streets and Multi-Use Pedestrian Paths Project.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ inquired as to what chemical compound is used
  for the slurry seal. Assistant City Manager Grammer noted he will find out and
  respond.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF asked if the entry portion of Monticello is included in
  the slurry seal project that is currently underway in the neighborhood.
  Assistant City Manager Grammer responded that, due to construction work
  adjacent to that portion of the roadway, it is not, but that it will be included in
  next year’s street maintenance program.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JUNE 14, 2016
   In response to COUNCILWOMAN HUFF, Planning Director Wahba stated he will
  inspect the temporary patch on Monticello for deterioration.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN HUFF, Assistant City Manager Grammer
  noted that there is a 10% contingency in the contract and that inspection and
  contract administration will be undertaken by Willdan Engineering.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN was pleased to note that this bid was below the budget
  estimate. He suggested that City Manager Prichard contact former Council
  Member Susan Seamans to thank her for making the City aware of need for
  repaving the off-street pedestrian/bike path as part of this project.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO AWARD THE BID TO ALL AMERICAN ASPHALT IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $1,039,695 FOR THE 2016 RESURFACING PROJECT ON VARIOUS CITY
  STREETS AND MULTI-USE PEDESTRIAN PATHS PROJECT.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell, Zerunyan

B.  APPROVE MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE PALOS
  VERDES PENINSULA CITIES RELATING TO PLACEMENT FOR AN
  AUTOMATED LICENSE PLATE RECOGNITION (ALPR) CAMERA REGIONAL
  SYSTEM

  Recommendation:  That the City Council approve the Memorandum of
  Understanding (MOU) between the Cities of Palos Verdes Estates, Rancho Palos
  Verdes, Rolling Hills, and Rolling Hills Estates relating to placement and
  maintenance of Automated License Plate Recognition (ALPR) cameras around
  the Palos Verdes Peninsula and approve the Rolling Hills Estates project cost in
  the amount of $80,247.54 for equipment and installation and $2,080 for
  ongoing cellular connectivity.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN HUFF’S concern regarding the number of
  cameras to be located in Rolling Hills Estates, Assistant to the City Manager
  Davis responded that the City has both the most and the largest intersections,
  and therefore, additional cameras are needed. She also reviewed the funding
  formula.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN HUFF regarding maintenance costs, Assistant
  to the City Manager Davis responded that there is a five-year warranty on the
  equipment.

  In response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN regarding who will monitor the system,
  Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated that the Sheriff’s Department would
  monitor the data and that various other departments will have access to this
  information as part of interagency cooperation common when investigating
  criminal activity.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ inquired if the City has the ability to obtain the
  data and wished to know who has primary ownership.

  Deputy City Attorney Thuyen noted that Section 6.3 refers to ownership of the
  data which states that the photos and data are the property of the City.

  City Manager Prichard commented that, as lead agency, Rancho Palos Verdes
  has the rights of ownership to the data through the contract language, but that
  Rolling Hills Estates would also have ownership rights through the
  Memorandum of Understanding.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JUNE 14, 2016
   COUNCILWOMAN HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING (MOU)
  BETWEEN THE CITIES OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES, RANCHO PALOS
  VERDES, ROLLING HILLS, AND ROLLING HILLS ESTATES RELATING TO
  PLACEMENT AND MAINTENANCE OF AUTOMATED LICENSE PLATE
  RECOGNITION (ALPR) CAMERAS AROUND THE PALOS VERDES
  PENINSULA AND APPROVED THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES PROJECT
  COST IN THE AMOUNT OF $80,247.54 FOR EQUIPMENT AND
  INSTALLATION AND $2,080 FOR ONGOING CELLULAR CONNECTIVITY.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell, Zerunyan

C.  APPROVAL OF CONTRACT WITH WESTERN A/V FOR AUDIOVISUAL AND
  BROADCAST SYSTEM UPGRADE

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize a contract for the
  Audiovisual and Broadcast Systems Upgrade Project with Western A/V in the
  amount of $111,920.52.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF inquired as to when this project will begin. Assistant
  to the City Manager Davis noted that a meeting has been scheduled with the
  firm in the next few days and that the project should commence over the
  summer and be completed by September.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF then inquired if there would be any disruption from
  this work. Assistant to the City Manager Davis responded that there should be
  minimal disruption as the Council Chambers is already wired, but that there
  may be a short period of time when broadcasting of meetings would not be
  possible.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN was pleased to note that this project also came in under
  budget.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO AUTHORIZE A CONTRACT FOR THE AUDIOVISUAL AND BROADCAST
  SYSTEMS UPGRADE PROJECT WITH WESTERN A/V IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $111,920.52.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell, Zerunyan

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

A.  CONTINUED PUBLIC HEARING INTRODUCING ORDINANCE NO. 705
  AMENDING CHAPTER 2.40 OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL
  CODE AND REVIEWING RESOLUTION NO. 2370 AMENDING THE CITY’S
  PERSONNEL RULES

  Recommendation: That the City Council Recommendation: That the City
  Council: 1) Continue to receive public testimony; 2) Discuss the issues; 3) Close
  the public hearing; 4) Conduct the second reading and adopt Ordinance No.
  705 amending Chapter 2.40; and 5) Approve Resolution No. 2370 amending
  Personnel Rules.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN invited any members of the audience to speak on this
  matter.

  No public testimony was offered.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JUNE 14, 2016
   COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 705 AND RESOLUTION NO. 2370.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell, Zerunyan

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN commended Assistant to the City Manager Davis for her
  extensive work on this project.

  City Manager Prichard read Ordinance No. 705 and Resolution No. 2370 by title
  only.

11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

A.  Kane Thuyen, Deputy City Attorney, noted his pleasure at attending this meeting.

12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS: This item provides the

A.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF MAY 23, 2016 – COUNCILWOMAN
  SCHMITZ

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted that discussion took place regarding the
  Mayor’s Breakfast Ride as it started late.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN further noted that this was the first year in which it proved

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

B.  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF reported that she attended the Council of Governments
  (COG) Steering Committee meeting where discussion took place regarding Metro’s

  and Gateway COGs will meet next week on this issue.

13.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS: This item provides the opportunity for Members

A.  AUTHORIZATION TO ATTEND LEAGUE OF CALIFORNIA CITIES ANNUAL
  CONFERENCE OCTOBER 5-7, 2016 – LONG BEACH

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN encouraged everyone to attend this conference since it is

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JUNE 14, 2016
   In response to COUNCILWOMAN HUFF regarding the cost of the League
  conference, COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ stated her belief that this conference
  would provide valuable information for all MEMBERS of the COUNCIL and
  encouraged attendance.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF moved, seconded COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO AUTHORIZE ATTENDANCE OF THOSE COUNCIL MEMBERS WHO
  WISH TO ATTEND THE 2016 LEAGUE OF CALIFORNIA CITIES ANNUAL

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

14.  CLOSED SESSION

  NONE
